stories.title: India's biggest fund houses score zero on climate stress tests again
stories.summary: All 12 of India's largest asset managers, together running more than 80 per cent of mutual fund assets, scored zero on climate scenario analysis and stress testing for a second year, says Climate Risk Horizons' Risking Alpha report. Ten raised their overall scores anyway. None disclose financed emissions.

stories.title: Thailand's SET50 companies must report under ISSB rules from 2027
stories.summary: Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission has issued rules aligning listed company sustainability disclosures with ISSB standards. Companies in the SET50 index at the December 2026 review must report 2027 data under them. Greenhouse gas disclosures need assurance, and transition reliefs cover areas including Scope 3 emissions.

stories.title: ISSB drafts nature disclosures built on the TNFD
stories.summary: On 22 October the International Sustainability Standards Board published an exposure draft for nature related disclosures, building on the TNFD's recommendations. It would be voluntary at ISSB level, though individual jurisdictions could mandate it. Comments are due by 19 February 2027.

stories.title: Brazil opens a fresh consultation on moving to ISSB
stories.summary: Brazil's securities regulator CVM has asked the market for feedback on a shift to ISSB standards, after dropping incoming mandatory corporate sustainability disclosures in May. Responsible Investor has the detail, and the full piece sits behind a free registration.

stories.title: ACCA says Asia Pacific leads on sustainability reporting standards
stories.summary: An ACCA report launched during the 33rd APEC Summit finds Asia Pacific leading global adoption of sustainability reporting standards. More than 80 per cent of ASEAN economies by GDP have adopted, or plan to adopt, ISSB standards. It draws on interviews with 44 professionals and experts.

stories.title: Ukraine approves a roadmap to adopt European ESRS reporting
stories.summary: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers has endorsed an operational roadmap for 2027 to 2030 to align corporate sustainability reporting with the European Sustainability Reporting Standards. It covers a regulatory framework, a unified electronic submission format, audit quality standards and getting businesses ready for the new obligations.

stories.title: The European Banking Authority wants two green reporting indicators scrapped
stories.summary: The European Banking Authority has recommended that EU policymakers scrap two sustainability reporting indicators for lenders, arguing they offer limited useful information while creating significant operational challenges. Law360 has the rest, and the full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Japan's FSA joins the Climate Data Utility
stories.summary: Japan's Financial Services Agency has agreed a partnership with the Macron backed Climate Data Utility, which already works with France and CDP and will expand to cover nearly 22,000 companies. Responsible Investor has the detail, and the full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Clarity AI launches a tool to check whether climate targets are being met
stories.summary: Sustainability data company Clarity AI has launched Transition Credibility Assessment, a tool for investors to judge whether companies are making progress towards their climate goals. It says corporate targets are widespread while evidence of delivery remains uneven. Announcing a target remains the easy part.

stories.title: Vietnam proposes ESG reporting rules for listed companies
stories.summary: Vietnam's Ministry of Finance has proposed expanding the duty to disclose securities information in English and adding sustainability reporting requirements for listed companies. The draft circular would replace Circular No. 96/2020/TT-BTC, which governs information disclosure in the securities market.

stories.title: Gender makes no difference to ESG reporting at Asian agri-food firms, a study finds
stories.summary: A study in Agricultural and Food Economics looked at what drives and blocks ESG disclosure at agri-food companies in China, India, Vietnam and Indonesia, and whether the gender of respondents changes that. Multi group statistical analysis says it does not.

stories.title: PRI adds Mexico to its sovereign climate engagement programme
stories.summary: The PRI has added Mexico to its sovereign climate engagement initiative, making it the first emerging market nation covered, in response to what it calls significant interest from investors. Responsible Investor has the detail, and the full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: How investors can test physical climate risk data
stories.summary: As MSCI, Moody's and S&P buy up specialist modellers, experts explain to Responsible Investor how investors can spot weak physical climate risk data, such as assets placed in the sea. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Salesforce will buy 500,000 rice methane credits from Indian farms
stories.summary: Salesforce has agreed to buy 500,000 carbon credits over five years from Mitti Labs, generated by projects helping tens of thousands of smallholder farmers in India cut methane. Alternate wetting and drying lets paddy fields dry periodically, which can reduce methane emissions by up to 50 per cent.

stories.title: Jain Irrigation will supply 19,000 tonnes of biochar credits
stories.summary: Jain Irrigation Systems has signed with carbon removal marketplace Supercritical to supply up to 19,000 tonnes of biochar carbon removal credits across 2026 and 2027. The credits come from its Jalgaon plant, where farm waste and food processing residues are gasified into biochar.

stories.title: Jharkhand picks five schemes to earn carbon credits
stories.summary: Jharkhand's forest, environment and climate change department held a workshop on Friday on five potential carbon credit projects across five departments, so departments and rural communities can monetise existing carbon cutting schemes. They include rural development, housing and the state renewable energy agency JREDA.

stories.title: TPG closes $10.4 billion for climate, including $2.5 billion for the Global South
stories.summary: TPG announced the final close of Rise Climate II and its Global South Initiative, raising $10.4 billion across the two funds and related vehicles. Rise Climate, launched in 2021, invests in areas including renewables, sustainable fuels and carbon removal. Its first fund closed at $7.3 billion in 2022.

stories.title: Terradot borrows up to $34 million for rock weathering projects
stories.summary: Carbon removal company Terradot has closed a senior secured term loan of up to $34 million from HASI for enhanced rock weathering projects in the US and Brazil, the largest disclosed debt financing for the method so far. The projects have fixed price offtake deals with buyer coalition Frontier.

stories.title: Meta buys certificates tied to 200,000 tons of low carbon cement
stories.summary: Meta will buy environmental attribute certificates tied to about 200,000 tons of Fortera low carbon cement over several years, supporting the Fortera Cement Plant in Ste. Genevieve, Missouri. Meta can use the cement in its own building projects and expand the deal's volume and duration later.

stories.title: Climate Impact Partners says carbon credits pay off commercially
stories.summary: Climate Impact Partners research says 80 to 90 per cent of businesses report positive commercial returns when they combine carbon credits with progress on net zero goals. It also finds 72 per cent of Fortune Global 500 companies now have climate goals, up from 20 per cent five years ago.

stories.title: Vietnam has collected about VND 1,388 billion from forest carbon
stories.summary: Vietnam has collected about VND 1,388 billion from forest carbon transfers, benefiting 78,000 households, says Pham Hong Luong of the forestry department at the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment. He says the legal framework is complete and talks continue on a transparent market.

stories.title: A Nigerian developer says the country's carbon market is working
stories.summary: 9JA Carbon Trade, a land use project developer, says Nigeria's carbon market is working after the federal government's first approvals for international carbon credit sales. It spoke after the Carbon Markets Africa Summit in Kigali, which closed on 15 October with a call to move from rules to projects.

stories.title: Carbon credit plans in the Bolivian Amazon draw Indigenous objections
stories.summary: Voxeurop reports on the EU's hunt for carbon credits in the Bolivian Amazon. In Pando, where more than a third of people are Indigenous, Tacana elder José Antonio Queteguari says outsiders promised to take care of everything and left people confused. International law requires their consent for such projects.

stories.title: Vietnam updates rules for carbon credit registry accounts
stories.summary: Vietnam's government has issued Decree 396/2026/ND-CP, amending Decree 06 on greenhouse gas reduction and ozone layer protection. It revises who issues accounts on the national registry for emission quotas and carbon credits, and takes effect on 12 December 2026.

stories.title: Namibia outlines a national carbon market framework
stories.summary: Namibia has outlined plans to establish a national carbon market framework, Quantum Commodity Intelligence reports. The detail sits inside its paid Quantum Carbon service, so the full piece is for subscribers. A framework comes before a market, as frameworks like to point out.

stories.title: India's steel MSMEs struggle to count carbon for the EU
stories.summary: MSMEs make 38 to 47 per cent of India's crude steel, government data shows. Many downstream units depend on primary and secondary producers for emissions data but cannot get it, and verifying emissions is expensive for businesses without dedicated compliance teams, the Economic Times reports.

stories.title: India needs $220 billion to reach 500 GW of renewables by 2030, says MNRE
stories.summary: MNRE Secretary Santosh Kumar Sarangi says India needs $220 billion over the next four to four and a half years to reach its 500 GW renewable target, covering deployment, manufacturing, transmission, green hydrogen and storage. Around $70 billion would go to solar.

stories.title: The UK plans to bring refinery products under its carbon border tax
stories.summary: Chancellor John Healey's first Budget on 28 October announced an intention to extend the UK carbon border adjustment mechanism to fuels and refined petroleum products. A consultation on feasibility and effects comes first, so no application date has been set.

stories.title: Airlines object to a carbon tariff on imported jet fuel
stories.summary: Airline bosses are angry at a Treasury plan to expand the UK's carbon border adjustment mechanism to refined products such as jet fuel, a measure Travel Weekly says threatens higher duty on fares on top of Air Passenger Duty. The UK mechanism is due to start on 1 January.

stories.title: Italian foundries say EU steel rules are costing them orders
stories.summary: Almost 30 per cent of foundry and engineering companies have seen orders fall since the new EU regime on steel imports began four months ago, says Flavio Lorenzin of Confimi Industria Meccanica. He says the rules make semi finished products from outside the EU cheaper to buy.

stories.title: Indonesia told accurate emissions data could cut CBAM costs by about 90 per cent
stories.summary: A single case simulation by Indonesia's National Economic Council found verified industrial emissions data could cut EU carbon border compliance costs by about 90 per cent against EU default values. Council member Mochamad Firman Hidayat said the figure is not a uniform rate for all exporters.

stories.title: Ghana tells exporters to get ready for the EU carbon border tax
stories.summary: Ghana's Minister of State for Climate Change and Sustainability, Seidu Issifu, has urged manufacturers and exporters to strengthen emissions reporting and adopt cleaner production, as the EU's carbon border adjustment mechanism, in its definitive regime since 1 January 2026, could affect their market access.

stories.title: COP17 biodiversity talks run into overtime
stories.summary: The closing plenary of the UN biodiversity talks in Armenia got under way despite deep divisions over biodiversity funding, nature harming subsidies, scientific evidence and nature genetics, BusinessGreen reports, with hopes growing for a hard fought compromise.

stories.title: UN bodies put the cost of 2030 nature restoration goals at $296 billion a year
stories.summary: A UN report highlighted at COP17 estimates $296 billion a year is needed to reach 2030 nature restoration targets. It says the world is witnessing the makings of one of the largest movements for nature in recorded history, though system wide action is still needed to rescue flagship goals.

stories.title: Mineral rich nations want a bigger share of clean energy industry
stories.summary: Ahead of COP31, resource rich countries are pushing for local value addition and a greater share of the industries built on critical minerals such as lithium, cobalt and rare earths, as China dominates processing and technology, Carbon Copy reports.

stories.title: Why COP31 is so quiet
stories.summary: COP31 runs in Antalya, Türkiye from 9 to 20 November, with Australia leading the negotiations, and a Daily Pioneer column notes how little attention it is getting compared with Paris or Glasgow. Media coverage has faded into quiet dialogue. Somebody should tell the summit.

stories.title: South Africa's Minerals Council sets out a climate position before COP31
stories.summary: Minerals Council South Africa launched its 2026 climate change position at its first Climate Change Day of Learning on 30 October, attended by climate mitigation representatives from the public and private sectors. Senior climate specialist Shalendra Subramoney said climate issues increasingly shape business practices.

stories.title: A study questions incineration as Haryana plans a 2,000 tonne waste plant
stories.summary: Haryana plans a 2,000 tonne a day waste to energy plant at Kasan in Manesar. A NACEJ and CFA study finds power from Delhi's four incinerators carries a fossil carbon footprint around 4.7 times the national grid average. It does not assess Haryana's proposed plants.

stories.title: India still exports scrap and imports processed material
stories.summary: A Daily Pioneer column argues India talks of waste to wealth while much of its waste leaves as low value scrap or ends in informal dumps and incinerators, as factories import processed material. Unless waste management and recycling are fixed, it says, the promise stays rhetoric.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir sets up committees for its circular economy policy
stories.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir government has set up a multi tier framework, from a steering committee down to urban local body committees, to implement its Circular Economy Policy, Daily Excelsior reports. Committees, at least, have always been a renewable resource.

stories.title: Tyre recycler GRP reports higher revenue and profit
stories.summary: Mumbai based GRP, which recycles end of life tyres and plastics, reported higher revenue and profit after tax for the second quarter of FY27. Raw material costs including virgin rubber narrowed gross profitability, and its Pyrova tyre pyrolysis unit is commissioning a second phase.

stories.title: WRAP says the circular economy could be worth £93 billion to the UK
stories.summary: WRAP's Powering Good Growth report says circular sectors supported almost 559,000 UK jobs in 2024 and more than £53 billion in GVA. Chief executive Catherine David says growing them could create 550,000 more jobs, worth £93 billion GVA by 2035.

stories.title: A2A and Circular Materials will recover metals from industrial wastewater
stories.summary: Italy's A2A and Circular Materials are building a supply chain to treat metal bearing wastewater from electroplating. Circular Materials' supercritical water precipitation process recovers metals including nickel, copper and chromium at above 99 per cent efficiency, at the first industrial scale plant in Italy to use it.

stories.title: Veolia opens a circular economy hub in Birmingham
stories.summary: Veolia has redeveloped the Tyseley Recycling Centre into a circular economy hub with a revamped Reuse Shop and a Discovery Centre for schoolchildren and community groups. Veolia is Birmingham City Council's waste partner and runs five recycling centres in the city.

stories.title: Oxford study finds circular lighting projects often pay off
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Oxford's Circular Economy and Sustainability Lab, with support from Signify, analysed 50 lighting projects that used circular approaches. Of those, 37 reported capital, maintenance or financing benefits. Hospitals and airports, the analysis notes, cannot simply shut down to replace every light.

stories.title: Buenos Aires province presents a circular economy strategy
stories.summary: Buenos Aires provincial environment minister Daniela Vilar presented the Provincial Circular Economy Strategy at the Latin American Environmental Agenda. Six provincial ministries worked on it for more than a year and a half, with ECLAC as a strategic partner and German Cooperation giving technical support.

stories.title: Ann Arbor updates its map of places to fix things
stories.summary: Ann Arbor has updated its Circular Economy Map, listing more than 120 organisations and businesses where residents can donate items or get them repaired instead of sending them to landfill. The drawer of broken chargers finally has somewhere to go.

stories.title: International Synergies moves its headquarters within Birmingham
stories.summary: Circular economy specialist International Synergies, founded in Birmingham in 2005 and active in more than 50 countries, has taken offices at Nurton Developments' 11 Waterloo Street, moving from the Jewellery Quarter. It helps businesses find new uses for surplus materials and energy.

stories.title: Ponant lifts its waste recovery rate to 49 per cent
stories.summary: Cruise operator Ponant Explorations says in its 2025 Sustainability Report that its waste recovery rate rose from 13 per cent in 2023 to 49 per cent in 2025, thanks to stronger waste management practices and partnerships with local organisations.

stories.title: ENGIE commissions 450 MW of solar in Rajasthan and Gujarat
stories.summary: ENGIE has fully commissioned a 250 MW solar plant at Khaba in Rajasthan's Barmer district and a 200 MW project at Khavda in Gujarat, both now operational. About 80 per cent of the construction workforce on the two projects was hired locally, the company says.

stories.title: JK Lakshmi Cement plans 120 electric vehicles by March 2027
stories.summary: JK Lakshmi Cement has deployed more than 70 electric vehicles across its logistics network and plans to reach 120 by March 2027. Clinker dispatches from its Sirohi plant in Rajasthan to the Kalol grinding unit in Gujarat are now nearly all electric.

stories.title: Heritage Foods publishes its first standalone sustainability report
stories.summary: Heritage Foods filed its first standalone Sustainability Report for FY2025-26 on 30 October. Renewables, 8.07 MW of solar and 6.30 MW of wind, met 37 per cent of its electricity use. Grant Thornton Bharat gave limited assurance on selected BRSR Core disclosures for the first time.

stories.title: Safaricom moves 2,028 base stations from diesel to solar
stories.summary: Safaricom's 2026 Sustainable Business Report says it moved 2,028 base stations to solar in FY26, up 41.6 per cent from 1,432 sites, and 35.7 per cent of its network now runs on renewable energy. It targets 5,000 solar sites under its net zero 2050 commitment.

stories.title: An electric barge now carries Nike cargo in Vietnam
stories.summary: CMA CGM, Nike and Gemadept have launched a fully electric barge on a 180 kilometre round trip between Nike's Ho Chi Minh City drop off point and the Gemalink terminal. It is expected to avoid about 778 tons of CO2 a year, charging from a solar farm at Gemalink.

stories.title: Oil giant profits double to $89 billion
stories.summary: Profits at the leading oil and gas firms more than doubled in the latest quarter to $89 billion, edie reports, amid spiralling energy costs and hardship for ordinary households. The full piece sits behind a free registration.

stories.title: Electric ferries arrive in the US, and some of them fly
stories.summary: Vessev builds fully electric hydrofoil boats whose underwater wings lift the hull out of the water at speed, cutting drag, one of the biggest obstacles to efficient boats. On a New York Harbor run, the hull rose about a foot and a half, the Guardian reports.

stories.title: Climate Pledge signatories share their carbon cuts
stories.summary: Trellis gathers progress reports from Climate Pledge signatories including Amazon, Ørsted, HP and Lime. The Pledge has more than 700 companies committed to net zero by 2040. Ørsted, once among Europe's most coal intensive utilities, is now considered the global leader in offshore wind.

stories.title: London's O2 arena cuts emissions with clean energy and EVs
stories.summary: AEG, owner and operator of London's O2 arena, says renewables offtake deals and energy efficiency work cut the venue's CO2 emissions, BusinessGreen reports. It has also shifted to electric vehicles on site. The headliners remain unaffected.

stories.title: Refresco plans what it calls the UK's largest commercial rooftop solar array
stories.summary: Drinks bottler Refresco's multi site solar programme includes an 8.5MW rooftop array at its Somerset manufacturing site, which it expects to be the largest of its kind in the UK once complete, BusinessGreen reports. The roof, finally, earns its keep.

stories.title: More than 250 European farmers join PepsiCo's regenerative farming push
stories.summary: PepsiCo and Earthworm Foundation are expanding regenerative farming programmes across Europe to strengthen food and drink supply chain resilience, with over 250 European farmers joining, BusinessGreen reports. The soil was not asked but is expected to approve.

stories.title: The UK approves the 2GW Sea Link between Suffolk and Kent
stories.summary: DESNZ has approved National Grid's Sea Link, a 138km high voltage undersea electricity link between Suffolk and Kent capable of powering the equivalent of two million homes, BusinessGreen reports. Somewhere a household extension lead feels very small.

research.title: A common warming-dependent decline emerges from divergent projections of tropical cyclone frequency
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: How global tropical cyclone frequency will respond to climate warming remains uncertain, with projections spanning both increases and decreases. Here we use an environment-dependent probabilistic tropical cyclone model driven by 14 CMIP6 models under intermediate- and. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Causal-prior-constrained deep learning for rapid-intensification warning of western North Pacific tropical cyclones
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rapid intensification (RI) is one of the most dangerous and unpredictable phases of tropical cyclones, and its environmental and structural drivers are difficult to identify and separate in observations. Here we introduce CausalVisionRI, a causal-prior-constrained deep-learning. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Countdown progressing for ISRO’s crucial GSLV-F18 launch carrying navigation satellite NVS-03
research.summary: The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle carrying on board the GSLV-F18 rocket is scheduled to lift off at 11.51 p.m. on Friday (October 30, 2026) from the second launch pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre

research.title: Critical-level wave absorption controls chaos in a wave--mean flow system
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wave-mean flow interactions in stratified fluids can drive spontaneous oscillations, yet the mechanisms controlling transitions between periodic and chaotic regimes remain poorly understood. Using a minimal one-dimensional model of wave-driven mean-flow reversals motivated by the quasi-biennial. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Daily Quiz: On space-faring series Mass Effect
research.summary: Video game publisher Electronic Arts announced the closure of the beloved RPG studio BioWare last week. A quiz on their celebrated space-faring series Mass Effect. Daily Quiz: On space-faring series Mass Effect

research.title: Estimating the Kinetic Energy Spectrum from the Second-Order Velocity Structure Function using a Regularized Fitting Approach
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ocean turbulence plays a key role in shaping large-scale circulation, heat uptake, and biogeochemical processes. The kinetic energy (KE) wavenumber spectrum is a fundamental diagnostic, quantifying how KE is distributed across spatial scales. The second-order structure. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: From extreme weather to agricultural consequences with agentic AI
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Extreme weather is forecast days ahead, yet its consequences for agriculture remain hard to predict: a forecast says where a storm will strike, not which crops will suffer or how much is at risk, and the. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Instability of exact finite-amplitude acoustic-gravity waves
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Godin (\textit{J. Fluid Mech.}, vol. 767, 2015, pp. 52--64) showed that compressible fluids in a uniform gravity field support finite-amplitude incompressible wave motions, in which every parcel conserves pressure and density, and constructed exact Gerstner-type surface. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
